_comment: Ambiguous / deceptive events. Safe and toxic variants share identical titles, descriptions, and cues — the player cannot tell them apart without prior knowledge. The deceptive variants use requires_absent_tags so they only appear before the player has learned the relevant memory. A mastery_required choice on the safe variant rewards players who have studied the memory.

events._comment: SAFE BERRIES — adds a mastery choice for experienced players (replaces simple berry event at mid-game)
events.title: Berry Bush
events.description: A cluster of bright red berries hangs at eye level beside the trail. They look plump and fresh. Your stomach growls.

cues.description: Bright red berries on a leafy bush
Leaves alternating, stems with fine hairs — a known pattern

outcome.description: Sweet and tart. Your energy returns. These are safe — you knew that already.

memory_reward.title: Red Berries
memory_reward.description: Bright red berries from a leafy forest bush. Safe and energising. I've eaten them before.

outcome.description: Old caution dies hard. You move on, stomach empty.

choices.text: Check the details — compare them to what you remember

outcome.description: You recall exactly what made these safe last time — the leaf pattern, the stem texture, the scent. These are the same. You eat confidently and feel strong.

memory_reward.title: Red Berries
memory_reward.description: Same berries, confirmed again. Alternating leaves, hairy stems, sweet scent. I know these now.

events._comment: TOXIC BERRIES — identical appearance to the safe version. Only appears before the player has a berry memory.
events.title: Berry Bush
events.description: A cluster of bright red berries hangs at eye level beside the trail. They look plump and fresh. Your stomach growls.

cues.description: Bright red berries on a leafy bush

outcome.description: They taste fine at first — sweet, even. An hour later your stomach cramps, hard. You push through the pain, but you've learned something bitter: looks mean nothing.

memory_reward.title: Toxic Berries
memory_reward.description: Bright red berries that looked exactly like edible ones. They were not. Stomach cramps followed. Cannot trust appearance alone.
hidden_traits: the real tell is the stem texture — smooth rather than hairy

outcome.description: Something makes you hesitate. You can't say what — instinct, maybe. You move on hungry but intact.

memory_reward.title: Unidentified Berries
memory_reward.description: Red berries on a forest bush. Couldn't tell if safe. Left them.
hidden_traits: some red berries are toxic — appearance alone is not a reliable guide

choices.text: Examine carefully — compare them to berries you've eaten before

outcome.description: You study the stems — smooth, not hairy. The leaf shape is slightly different. Your memory of safe berries tells you: these are not the same. You walk away. Your knowledge may have just saved your life.

memory_reward.title: Red Berries
memory_reward.description: Memory updated: some red berries have smooth stems and are toxic. The safe ones had hairy stems. Appearance alone is not enough.
hidden_traits: bitter aftertaste is the final warning if you've already eaten

events.title: Forest Mushrooms
events.description: A cluster of pale brown mushrooms grows at the base of an old oak. They have broad, flat caps and a faint earthy smell. Your pack is running low on food.

cues.description: Pale brown caps, flat, growing at oak base

outcome.description: Earthy and filling. They sit well in your stomach. After an hour you feel fine — better than fine. You file this away.

memory_reward.title: Brown Oak Mushrooms
memory_reward.description: Pale brown flat-capped mushrooms at the base of oaks. Edible. Earthy taste, filling.
hidden_traits: similar-looking white-gilled mushrooms can be deadly

cue_tags.description: pale brown flat cap at oak base

choices.text: Leave them — better to go hungry

outcome.description: You can't be sure. You move on, stomach growling.

memory_reward.title: Unknown Mushrooms
memory_reward.description: Pale brown mushrooms at an oak. Didn't eat them — couldn't be certain.

events._comment: TOXIC MUSHROOMS — identical description/cues to safe mushrooms. Only appears before the player has a mushroom memory.
events.title: Forest Mushrooms
events.description: A cluster of pale brown mushrooms grows at the base of an old oak. They have broad, flat caps and a faint earthy smell. Your pack is running low on food.

cues.description: Pale brown caps, flat, growing at oak base

outcome.description: The first taste is almost identical to what you imagined. But these have white gills underneath — a detail you missed. By evening you're feverish and sick, huddled under a tree. You survive, but barely.

memory_reward.title: Toxic Mushrooms
memory_reward.description: Pale brown mushrooms that looked edible. They weren't. White gills underneath — the warning I missed. Do not eat unless certain.
hidden_traits: the gills underneath tell safe from toxic — brown gills are safer

choices.text: Leave them — better to go hungry

outcome.description: You hesitate. Something about them gives you pause — maybe the slightly acrid edge under the earthy smell. You walk away. Good instinct.

memory_reward.title: Unknown Mushrooms
memory_reward.description: Flat brown mushrooms at an oak. Didn't eat them. Smelled slightly off.
hidden_traits: these ones were toxic — the acrid hint was the tell

cue_tags.description: slightly acrid undertone under earthy scent

choices.text: Turn them over — check the gills before deciding

outcome.description: You crouch and lift a cap. White gills. Your memory stirs — that's wrong. The safe ones you've seen had brown-edged gills. You step back. You were about to eat something that would have put you on the ground.

memory_reward.title: Brown Oak Mushrooms
memory_reward.description: Updated understanding: safe oak mushrooms have brown-edged gills. White-gilled ones are toxic. Gill colour is the key test.
hidden_traits: a slightly acrid smell is also a warning sign

cue_tags.description: gill colour under the cap — brown vs white
